noodle_queen.judgment: TASTE+FUNCTION+CONTEMPT PASS: the deep split coil, compact two-anchor hinge, diagonal airborne partner, release fork, collapsed recoil, and forward overshoot are distinct silhouettes; force/contact ownership is embodied rather than caption-dependent; transfer and release are coherent; recovery carries visible debt; the animation is economical without looking like placeholder mannequins or tween sludge.

iterations.correction: Reduce the force visualization to a local >X< hinge around the shared center and compare anchor endpoint/owner identity rather than changing anchor coordinates, so K3->K4 and K5->K6 compile actual locked curved relationship motion without changing contact/support/custody events.
iterations.highest_value_visible_defect: The contact core reads as a dense horizontal force-bar that obscures both bodies and the lock/load silhouette; the intended locked curved bridges also fail to compile because anchor coordinates were incorrectly treated as topology identity.

iterations.correction: On every LOCKED_POLAR bridge, snap both authored endpoint joints to the same interpolated anchor coordinate while preserving shared-center motion and planted-support geometry.
iterations.highest_value_visible_defect: Locked bridge frames preserve relationship state in metadata but the rendered grip endpoints can drift away from the moving anchor marker, making ownership briefly float during leverage and throw.

iterations.judgment: Actual movie and decisive/bridge frame inspection show an asymmetric low approach, distinct first/second acquisition, readable >X< relationship hinge, opposing leverage arcs, support loss only after load, a curved locked throw, explicit release gap, divergent partner lag/carrier recoil, forward overshoot, authored ground consequence, and recovery debt. No material symmetry, equal-spacing, straight semantic tween, floating anchor, ownership ambiguity, reverse interpolation, or idle-reset defect remains.

principle: CONTACT IS A SCOPED SYNCHRONIZATION CONTRACT: approach remains asymmetric and local; acquisition creates explicit anchors and a shared force center; leverage changes support/root consequences before release; release destroys the relationship frame; recoil, partner lag, overshoot, settle, and recovery debt remain on separate local clocks.
